title: The Rising of the Shield Hero
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Naofumi Iwatani is summoned to a fantasy world as one of four Cardinal Heroes, but receives only a shield and is scorned as weak. His sole companion, the kingdom's princess, robs him and falsely accuses him of sexual assault, leaving him disgraced and bitter. Naofumi buys a demi-human slave girl, Raphtalia, and later raises the bird-monster Filo; as they fight the destructive Waves together, trust and a found family slowly heal him.
life_message: It holds up loyalty, earned trust and protecting those society discards, after betrayal has broken faith in others.

content.note: Monster battles with biting, slashing and lots of blood; parents torn apart in a flashback; duels (CSM 15+ on the anime; UK Anime Network; Wikipedia).
Slavery shown as frightening; betrayal and public disgrace; Waves of monsters (CSM; Wikipedia; AniList Bullying 80%, Fugitive).
Central false rape accusation; slave virginity priced; brief nudity in a hot spring and shapeshifting; lolicon jokes (Wikipedia; CSM; UK Anime Network; MangaUpdates Rape category).
CSM lists 'bastard', 'whore', 'bitch', 's--t' in the anime; manga level to verify.
Wine drinking and pressure to drink (CSM on the anime).
Naofumi's trauma and cynicism after betrayal (loss of taste, to verify); Raphtalia's trauma as an enslaved orphan (Wikipedia; UK Anime Network; CSM).
Buying a slave is presented as a necessity for the hero; critics debated the false-accusation premise (UK Anime Network; Wikipedia).

delivery.note: The hero's grievance drives the story, and critics debate how its premise frames the accuser.

winners_losers: Naofumi and his loyal companions win; the lying princess, a corrupt state church and arrogant fellow heroes lose. Sympathy goes to the wrongfully accused outsider.
